newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks details on possible veto targets.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks details on possible veto targets.

text.p: President Bill Clinton Friday sought additional details on items in the budget package that could be targets of the first line-item veto ever issued from the White House.
Clinton this week signed signed a budget bill intended to balance the budget by 2002 and a companion piece that cuts taxes by a net $95 billion over five years.
He has until midnight Monday to strike certain provisions from the measures.
"The president has not made a decision" on whether he will veto any provisions in the budget and tax legislation approved by Congress, White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said.
"He has indicated to some people here he wants to get this right," McCurry said, noting that a president's ability to remove specific provisions from a bill began this year and has yet to be used.

"So this being the first time, if it is to be the first time, the president wants to assure that it's done properly," he said. "And he wants to think very carefully about the circumstances in which he would use this authority."
McCurry said "there are only a handful of provisions that he's looking at and...some of them go in and out of focus, depending on additional information that we get."

He said Clinton had asked his economic advisers -- who are divided over the wisdom of vetoing legislation that won wide bi-partisan support in Congress -- for additional information on potential veto targets.
